answer: Persistent work-history beacon: each identity accumulates a signed task ledger; rewards unlock only after counterparties co-sign completed work. A new clone starts with an empty ledger, so it earns nothing until real work is done. Auditors whisper cross-checks between ledgers, and a pigment hash ties each entry to its origin so copied histories fail verification. Cloning thus costs the full labor of rebuilding a ledger plus forfeited earnings during the wait.
